user.title: Where do you walk the dog?
user.description: Rain is predicted for a circle around this point. Move the marker from your Home Assistant home location if you usually walk somewhere else.

schedule_mode.title: Walk schedule
schedule_mode.description: How do you want to describe your walk times?

schedule_times.title: Walk times
schedule_times.description: Add the time each walk usually starts. A day with no walks can be left empty, as long as there is at least one walk somewhere in the week.

walk_target.title: Who is told about this walk?
walk_target.description:
**Walk {index} of {total}: {days} at {time}.**

Everything on this page applies to this walk time only — {days} at {time}. The wizard asks again for each walk you configured.

Its alert always goes to {default_device}. The fields below only add to that: more phones for this one walk, a switch that silences them, and the person whose absence silences them.

data.mute: Do not notify this walk's phones
data.away_entity: Skip this walk's phones while this person is away

data_description.notify_services: Phones notified about this one walk on top of the always-notified device. A phone whose tracker says it is not home is skipped; the others are still notified. Leave empty if this walk needs no extra phone.
data_description.mute: The phones listed above get no notification about this walk. The always-notified device still does — only the Alerting switch stops that one. The sensor and the walk_the_dog_alert event keep updating either way.
data_description.away_entity: Applies only to this walk's phones that have no tracker of their own. Leave empty to use the person from Alert settings.

params.title: Alert settings
params.description: How far around the walk location to look, what counts as rain, and how far the suggested walk time may move.

data.confirm_margin_min: Second message shortly before you leave
data.auto_mute_entity: Skip phones while this person is away

data_description.radius_km: The circle around the walk location that is checked for rain.
data_description.intensity_threshold: A moment counts as rainy once the forecast reaches this intensity.
data_description.earlier_margin_min: How much earlier than the scheduled time you are willing to set off. This is also when the notification arrives, so keep it at 60 minutes or less: that is as far ahead as the rain radars forecast, and a message sent earlier than that can only be based on hourly models.
data_description.later_margin_min: How much later than the scheduled time you are willing to set off. Going later is always checked again as the time approaches — the radars will have seen it long before you have to leave — so a wide margin here costs nothing but a few more forecast requests.
data_description.walk_duration_min: How long a walk takes. The whole walk has to stay dry for a time to be suggested, so a walk longer than the 60 minutes the radars forecast can never be fully radar-backed at the moment you are told to go.
data_description.confirm_margin_min: A second, short message this many minutes before you actually set off, saying that the plan you were given still stands — or that the rain has gone and you can walk at the normal time after all. It goes to the same devices as the first message. 0 switches it off, which is the default: no news already means nothing has changed.
data_description.notify_service: The companion app device that receives every walk's alert. Nothing silences it — not being away, not muting a single walk — except the Alerting switch. Phones added to an individual walk are notified alongside it. Leave empty to notify only the per-walk phones.
data_description.fire_event: Fires the walk_the_dog_alert event so your own automations can react.
data_description.auto_mute_entity: A fallback presence rule for phones that cannot say where they are. A companion app phone has a tracker of its own and answers for itself; only a phone without one asks about this person, and falls silent while they are away. The always-notified device is never affected.

long_walk.title: That is a long walk
long_walk.description: You entered {duration} minutes. The rain radars forecast {horizon} minutes ahead, and beyond that only hourly models are left, so for walks over {limit} minutes the suggestion will more often be a best guess. Confirm to keep this duration, or leave it unconfirmed to go back and change it.

beyond_radar.title: The alert lands before the radar can see it
beyond_radar.description:
You asked to be told {earlier} minutes before the walk. The rain radars only forecast {horizon} minutes ahead, so at that moment nothing has looked at your walk time yet and the first message rests on hourly weather models — reliable about whether it will rain, vague about the exact minute it starts.

That is not useless, and the integration keeps watching: as the walk comes within radar range it re-checks and tells you again if the answer changes. But a margin of {horizon} minutes or less gets a radar-backed answer straight away. Confirm to keep {earlier} minutes ({over} minutes past the radar's reach), or leave it unconfirmed to go back and lower it.

error.invalid_time: A walk time could not be read. Use the 24-hour form, for example 07:30.
error.no_walk_times: Add at least one walk time.
error.invalid_notify_service: Pick one of the listed devices, or type a notify service name that starts with mobile_app_.

options.per_day: Every day of the week is different

common.notification_earlier: Rain is expected around {scheduled}. Set off at {recommended} instead — {shift} minutes earlier — and the whole {duration}-minute walk should stay dry, back home by {until}.
common.notification_later: Rain is expected around {scheduled}. Wait until {recommended} — {shift} minutes later — and the whole {duration}-minute walk should stay dry, back home by {until}.
common.notification_provisional: The radar does not reach that far ahead yet, so this is a model estimate — I am still watching and will tell you if it changes.
common.notification_no_dry_window: Rain is expected around {scheduled} and there is no dry {duration}-minute window nearby. Take a raincoat.
common.notification_confirmed: Still on: set off at {recommended}, back home by {until}. Nothing has changed since the last message.
common.notification_stand_down: Rain is no longer expected around {scheduled} — walk at the normal time after all.
common.default_device_unset: whichever device you set as "Always notify this device" in Alert settings

walked.name: Already went
walked.description: Closes the walk being watched right now: no further advice about it, and no further weather requests for it. Alerting itself stays on, and the next walk is picked up as usual.

no_loaded_entry.message: Walk the dog is not set up, so there is no walk to close.
